notes: MCP TOOLS plus the HTTP sender other tool crates will build on. Read rever-tools-api/src/tool.rs and utils.rs first: implement `Tool` for each tool (`def()` returns `ToolDef::new("<name>", "<description>", <schema>)` with the name as a string literal at that call, the description copied verbatim from the TypeScript because it is prompt text, and the schema being the zod schema converted to JSON Schema: same property names, types, enums, defaults, limits, descriptions and required list), and expose `pub fn register(registry: &mut ToolRegistry)` from lib.rs. Output text must equal the TypeScript's: same wording, same JSON shape and key order (serde_json's preserve_order feature is enabled in this crate, keep it). repeater.ts replays a captured request with modifications through Electron's network stack: port it as a public async API of this crate (same function names in snake_case, same modification rules, redirects, timeouts, size caps and result shape) on reqwest with rustls-tls; cookies the browser would attach come from `ctx.browser.cookies(url)` when the TypeScript relied on the session's cookie jar, and a failure of that call (unsupported) means sending without them. Scope and fence checks before sending are already ported in rever-scope (scope, fence): use them exactly where the TypeScript does, since they are the safety boundary of Red Team scans. raw_http.ts speaks raw sockets (net and tls): use tokio TcpStream and tokio-rustls. grpc_call.ts frames gRPC-web messages: protobuf helpers are in rever-formats. State the TypeScript keeps in module variables goes in a struct fetched with `ctx.state::<T>()`. Tests must not reach the internet: start a local tokio TcpListener or axum server inside the test and send to 127.0.0.1. A tool file gets the `Port of` marker when all of its tools are registered.
